suggestion.problemOrOpportunity: npm test -- --review runs a machinery suite only when a path in its hand-kept source list changed. The lists omit files the suites execute: a behavior change in scripts/harness.mjs does not select harness-fixtures, the only suite that tests it, and the mutant passes every selected machinery suite. Six orders have already added entries by hand after the fact.
suggestion.scope: Add one check to the runner-fixtures suite: for each machinery suite, the entry file, its static first-party imports and the script paths it spawns must be covered by its declared sources, with a reasoned exclusion list for shared libraries the operator chooses to leave out. Then repair the lists the check reports. The selection rule itself stays as decided.
affectedUsers: executors whose final criterion names npm test -- --review
verifiers and reviewers who read a green --review as covering the change
planners who name re-mints and gates per order
suggestion.expectedValue: A green --review means every machinery suite that executes a changed file ran. List upkeep stops being a per-order hand step and a finding class at verification.
suggestion.uncertainty: The number of real gaps after shared libraries are excluded is unknown; the drill proves one. Covering transitive imports could select the two longest suites (harness-fixtures, process-debt) on most script changes and lengthen --review by minutes.
risks: Over-selection restores the long review gate that the machinery stand-down removed
A closure over spawned script paths needs a convention for paths built at run time
alternatives: Cover direct imports and spawned entry scripts only, leaving shared libraries to the product suites
Run npm run test:machinery once at final review regardless of selection
duplicationHints: WO-169 D007 and WO-173 D003 (untracked files join the selection)
suggestion.urgencyRationale: The review gate is the executable witness at implementation-ready and final review. Each order that adds a script widens the uncovered set, and first verifications already fail at about 40 to 50 per cent.
